text: A.J. Brown is inching toward activation after four games away from a right high ankle sprain, though Mike Vrabel will hold off on a final decision until Saturday, with Brown himself characterizing his status as still "up in the air"—a potentially crucial variable heading into Sunday's divisional showdown against the Jets, who arrive as upset candidates behind Geno Smith's impressive no-interception streak. Christian Gonzalez is expected to play through his injuries, while off the field, tight end Hunter Henry earned NFLPA Community MVP honors for hosting his second annual "Freedom to Play" ping pong tournament, making it back-to-back weeks the Patriots have had an award winner as Mack Hollins took home the recognition two weeks ago. The Jets view this as a "big-ass game" for their playoff positioning in what shapes up to be a pivotal AFC East clash at Gillette Stadium, even as New England is riding momentum from a 28-point blowout victory and gearing up specifically to counter New York's blitz-heavy defensive scheme.
